subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Which internal instruction-scope principles should become public policy, and should declared external or elevated behavior remain review-required rather than automatically allowed?
rationale: This changes ClawHub's public trust contract, moderation discretion, and author appeal expectations, so automation cannot safely select the boundary.

options.title: Publish principled boundary
options.body: Allow disclosed task-scoped instructions, require review for elevated or external execution, and prohibit hidden, unrelated, or confirmation-bypassing directions.

options.title: Ban external execution asks
options.body: Disallow all documentation-directed external execution regardless of disclosure or stated purpose.

options.title: Retain internal-only rules
options.body: Keep public policy general and leave instruction-scope decisions to internal scanning and reviewer judgment.

recommendation.title: Publish principled boundary
recommendation.body: Allow disclosed task-scoped instructions, require review for elevated or external execution, and prohibit hidden, unrelated, or confirmation-bypassing directions.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current public acceptable-use policy that is the strongest existing home for this rule.
